Winter – Spring 2026

BY Kelsie Jankowski

The Winter-Spring 2026 season at Swann saw multiple successes across our departments. Single-owner collections included fine photograph selections from A Country Called California: The Collection of Stephen White, African American art from the Estate of Dr. J. Eugene Grigsby, Jr., Important Signed Photographs from a California Family Collection, Highlights from the Gooding Family Collection of Posters, and illustration offerings from the Collection of David J. Holmes. Also of note was a special Semiquincentennial edition of our biannual Printed & Manuscript Americana auction.

Books & Manuscripts

The Books & Manuscripts department at Swann saw record-breaking prices across each of its auctions this past season. The year opened with the annual Printed & Manuscript African Americana; the top lots from this auction were an archive of material related to Coretta Scott King from her literary agent, Joan Daves ($55,880), and the 1961-62 edition of The Bronze American National Travel Guide, a competitor to the Green Book which was soon rendered obsolete due to the Civil Rights Act of 1964 ($21,590). Autographs were a strong performer this season, with the April sale featuring a letter signed by Thomas Jefferson, as Governor, to Major General Nathanael Greene ($25,400), and a single-owner collection which boasted signed photographs by John Wilkes Booth ($107,950) and Abraham Lincoln ($139,200). Printed & Manuscript Americana: Semiquincentennial Edition in late June rounded out this season’s exceptional books and manuscript offerings and was led by a letter signed by John Whitmer, one of the Eight Witnesses, affirming the Book of Mormon ($322,200).

Fine Art

The Fine Art department opened the Winter-Spring 2026 season with The Artists of the WPA, a season favorite among collectors that features artists who worked under the Works Progress Administration across mediums. Top lots from this season’s fine art offerings included standout works by women, including Margaret Hoening French’s Narcissus, tempera on wood panel, circa 1938 ($106,680), and Linda Lindeberg’s It Is, oil on canvas, 1958 ($68,850). Two landscapes by Richard Mayhew were among the top lots for African American Art: Scarlet Journey, oil on canvas, 2006 ($249,000), andSoquel, oil on canvas, 1994 ($249,000).Works on paper included Martin Lewis’sCircus Night, drypoint, 1933 ($25,400), and from Illustration Art, Ernest Howard Shepard‘s “As he sat on the grass and looked across the river…” a pen and ink drawing for The Wind in the Willows by Kenneth Grahame ($30,480).

Vintage Posters provided exciting surprises this season with a private collection and rarely seen advertisements. As the founder of the legendary printer and publisher Palm Press, Inc.,it’s a given that Gus Kayafas’ influence can be felt everywhere you turn in the photo world.But sit and talk with him for an hour, and you’ll walk away feeling educated and enlightened by his stories, experiences, and front row seat to the growing photography market from the 1970s on.

Kayafas attended MIT, where he studied under Minor White and Harold Edgerton, working intensely with both. Eventually, Kayafas’ career would become intertwined with Edgerton’s, the two becoming friends, and Kayafas the photographer’s printer, publisher, and steady collaborator. Kayafas then received his MFA in Photography from Rhode Island School of Design, studying with Harry Callahan and Aaron Siskind, and went on to establish MassArt’s photography program. Kayafas printed for Callahan and Siskind through the rest of their long and productive careers.

Palm Press, what Kayafas calls a “photographic atelier,” is known for high-quality printing and was founded in 1976. He has worked with thousands of photographers and other entities, producing more than 60 portfolios, and continuing to serve as an educational force in the community. Kayafas’ technical background also led to diverse experimentation with print processes and technology.

The Kayafas Collection ranges all the way from nineteenth-century to contemporary masters, an affectionate and voracious approach that can be seen in our upcoming April 30th auction. The diverse work is united by Kayafas’ unerring eye for elegance and beauty, and comes with a deep knowledge of the photographer’s body of work and approach to image-making. We are pleased to include work by Walker Evans, Frank Gohlke, Garry Winogrand, Helen Levitt, Peter Sekaer, Nicholas Nixon, Lee Friedlander, Rosalind Fox Solomon, Herb Greene, August Sander, and Robert Cottingham, among much more.

La historia está siendo hecha con el viaje de Artemis II alrededor de la luna.

He aquí un vistazo a las imágenes tomadas durante esos primeros viajes históricos y exploraciones espaciales.

A Alice Le Campion

Desde que empezamos a enviar humanos al espacio, las cámaras las han acompañado. Desde el icónico Earthrise hasta el primer retrato hecho en el espacio hasta la primera caminata espacial estadounidense, las cámaras sostenidas por astronautas han registrado el inmenso logro humano de la exploración espacial. Mientras esperamos el lanzamiento de Artemis II, marcando la primera misión humana de la luna en más de 50 años y el primer vuelo humano lunar, ofrecemos una mirada a las fotografías de la NASA incluidas en nuestro espacio del 30 de abril

¿Qué fotografías veremos de Artemis II? El lanzamiento histórico marca la primera vez que los astronautas viajarán más allá de la órbita terrestre baja desde 1972, incluyendo a la primera mujer a la luna. Esta misión pretende establecer una presencia a largo plazo en la Luna y allanar el camino para futuras exploraciones más allá de ella. También probará el viaje humano al espacio profundo y un retorno seguro.

*o puro decir la humanidad

El Primer Americano en el Espacio...

Bill Taub, NASA-Mercury-Redstone 3. La Primera Am e rico en el espacio — Alan Shepard Momentos antes de lanzar la libertad 75 de mayo de 1961.

Capturado por el fotógrafo superior de la NASA Bill Taub, este retrato íntimo no revela el espectáculo de la luz espacial, sino su umbral humano: concentración, resistencia y determinación silenciosa en el borde de lo desconocido. Momentos más tarde, ante una multitud de más de 500.000 espectadores, Shepard se convertiría en el primer estadounidense en viajar al espacio, inaugurando una nueva era de exploración y ambición geopolítica.

Ed White Floating sobre Hawai durante la primera caminata espacial estadounidense...

James McDivitt, NASA–Gemini IV. La primera fotografía de un Humano en el espacio: Ed White Floating sobre Hawai durante la primera caminata espacial estadounidense, 3-7 de junio de 1965.

Antes de esta fotografía, la presencia humana en el espacio sólo había sido vislumbrada a través de imágenes en movimiento —fleeting, inestable. Aquí, por primera vez, está fija y compuesta. Una vez una hazaña técnica y una obra maestra de composición fotográfica, esta imagen es uno de los iconos definidos de la Edad Espacial, un precursor de los aterrizajes de la Luna, y una de las primeras afirmaciones visuales que la humanidad había comenzado su viaje más allá de la Tierra.

La Primera Pasillo Espacial de Estados Unidos...

James McDivitt, NASA–Gemini IV. Ed White Tomando las primeras fotografías en el espacio exterior durante la primera caminata espacial estadounidense3-7 de junio de 1965.

Suspendido por encima del horizonte azul luminoso de la Tierra, el astronauta Ed White es capturado en el acto de fotografiar su entorno durante la primera pasarela americana. Fotografía por James McDivitt desde el interior de la nave espacial utilizando un Hasselblad modificado por la NASA 500C con película Ektachrome de 70 mm, esta imagen revela una profunda transformación: el astronauta se convierte en explorador y creador de imágenes.

Lanzamiento de los primeros humanos hacia otro mundo...

Ralph Morse, NASA–Apollo 8. Lanzamiento Histórico de los Primeros Humanos Hacia Otro Mundo21 de diciembre de 1968.

Más que un lanzamiento, esta imagen captura un umbral: el comienzo de la exploración humana en el espacio profundo, donde la Luna ya no es un objeto de observación, sino un destino.

Earthrise...

William Anders, NASA–Apollo 8. Primera Tierra: La Iconic First Color Photograph of Earthrise Taken by Humans, Diciembre 21–27, 1968.

El 24 de diciembre de 1968, cuando el Apolo 8 orbitó la Luna, la Tierra se levantó inesperadamente por encima del horizonte lunar estéril. Por primera vez, los ojos humanos —y una cámara humana— atestiguaron nuestro planeta de otro mundo. Anders capturarían lo que sería una de las fotografías más influyentes jamás hechas.

Primera fotografía de la Luna entera

William Anders,NASA–Apollo 8. La primera fotografía de la Luna entera tomada de una perspectiva ajena a la Tierra, 21 al 27 de diciembre de 1968.

La Luna, como ningún ser humano lo había visto antes. Por primera vez en la historia, una visión completa del globo lunar fue capturada por manos humanas desde un punto de vista fuera de la Tierra, revelando un hemisferio y una perspectiva inaccesibles desde nuestro planeta. Sólo al subir por encima de la Luna después de la primera maniobra de inyección trans-Tierra los astronautas del Apolo 8 presenciaron esta visión completa y unificada.

History is being made with Artemis II’s trip around the moon.

Here is a look at images taken during those first historic journeys and space explorations.

BY Alice Le Campion

Since we began sending humans into space, cameras have accompanied them. From the iconic Earthrise to the first portrait made in space to the first U.S. spacewalk, cameras held by astronauts have recorded the immense human achievement of space exploration. As we wait for the launch of Artemis II, marking the first human moon mission in over 50 years and the first human lunar flyby, we offer a look at NASA photographs included in our April 30th sale that celebrate mankind’s* achievements in space more than half a century ago.

What photographs will we see from Artemis II? The historic launch marks the first time astronauts will travel beyond low Earth orbit since 1972, including the first woman to the moon. This mission aims to establish a long-term presence on the Moon and pave the way for future explorations beyond it. It will also test human travel to deep space and a safe return.

*or should we say humankind

The First American in Space…

Bill Taub, NASA–Mercury-Redstone 3. The First Am e rican in Space — Alan Shepard Moments before Launch Aboard Freedom 7, May 5, 1961.

Captured by NASA’s senior photographer Bill Taub, this intimate portrait reveals not the spectacle of spaceflight, but its human threshold: concentration, endurance, and quiet determination at the edge of the unknown. Moments later, before a crowd of over 500,000 spectators, Shepard would become the first American to journey into space, inaugurating a new era of exploration and geopolitical ambition.

Ed White Floating over Hawaii during the First U.S. Spacewalk…

James McDivitt, NASA–Gemini IV. The First Photograph of a Human in Space: Ed White Floating over Hawaii during the First U.S. Spacewalk, June 3-7, 1965.

Before this photograph, human presence in space had only been glimpsed through moving images—fleeting, unstable. Here, for the first time, it is fixed and composed. At once a technical feat and a masterpiece of photographic composition, this image stands as one of the defining icons of the Space Age—a precursor to the Moon landings, and one of the earliest visual affirmations that humanity had begun its journey beyond Earth.

The First U.S. Spacewalk…

James McDivitt, NASA–Gemini IV. Ed White Taking the First Photographs in Outer Space during the First U.S. Spacewalk, June 3-7, 1965.

Suspended above the Earth’s luminous blue horizon, astronaut Ed White is captured in the act of photographing his surroundings during the first American spacewalk. Photographed by James McDivitt from inside the spacecraft using a NASA-modified Hasselblad 500C with 70mm Ektachrome film, this image reveals a profound transformation: the astronaut becomes both explorer and image-maker. White is no longer merely observing space—he is actively documenting it while immersed in its vacuum.

Launch of the First Humans Toward Another World…

Ralph Morse, NASA–Apollo 8. The Historic Launch of the First Humans Toward Another World, December 21, 1968.

More than a launch, this image captures a threshold: the beginning of deep-space human exploration, where the Moon is no longer an object of observation, but a destination.

Earthrise…

William Anders, NASA–Apollo 8. First Earthrise: The Iconic First Color Photograph of Earthrise Taken by Humans, December 21–27, 1968.

On December 24, 1968, as Apollo 8 orbited the Moon, Earth rose unexpectedly above the barren lunar horizon. For the first time, human eyes—and a human camera—witnessed our planet from another world. Anders would capture what would become one of the most influential photographs ever made.

First Photograph of the Whole Moon

William Anders,NASA–Apollo 8. The First Photograph of the Whole Moon Taken from a Perspective Other Than Earth, December 21–27, 1968.

The Moon, as no human had ever seen it before. For the first time in history, a complete view of the lunar globe was captured by human hands from a vantage point other than Earth—revealing a hemisphere and perspective inaccessible from our planet. Only upon rising above the Moon after the first trans-Earth injection maneuver did the Apollo 8 astronauts witness this full, unified vision.

29 de enero de 2026

POR Kelsie Jankowski

Swann Galleries inauguró el año con una subasta dedicada a los artistas de la WPA por quinto año consecutivo. «El departamento y el material en sí han alcanzado su plena madurez», señaló Nicholas D. Lowry, presidente de Swann. «Durante la puja, las ofertas fueron tan frenéticas y emocionantes como las que hemos vivido en los últimos años, con una participación muy activa en la sala». La venta recaudó 530 288 dólares, superando ligeramente su estimación previa de 520 300 dólares y vendiendo el 87 % de los lotes. «Sería fácil decir que hemos hecho bien nuestro trabajo y que estamos cosechando los frutos de toda la atención que hemos dedicado a este sector desatendido del mercado del arte; sin embargo, también es muy posible imaginar que el corazón y el alma del movimiento de la WPA, y en particular del Proyecto de Arte Federal —en el que el gobierno dio empleo a artistas para ayudar a combatir la Gran Depresión—, están siendo valorados de nuevo por personas de una nueva era. Sin duda, da la sensación de que las iniciativas del New Deal son disfrutadas por un público moderno por la misma razón que este arte resultaba tan cautivador cuando fue creado, aunque ahora con un matiz mucho más nostálgico», concluyó Lowry.

Fotografía de la FSA

Dorothea Lange, Madre migrante, Nipomo, California, copia a la gelatino-plata, 1936, positivada en la década de 1970. Vendida por 13 970 dólares.

La subasta estuvo encabezada por la icónica obra de Dorothea Lange Madre migrante, Nipomo, California (copia a la gelatino-plata de 1936, positivada en la década de 1970), que alcanzó los 13 970 dólares. Entre las fotografías adicionales de la FSA destacaron The American Way of Life (At the Time of the Louisville Flood, Kentucky) de Margaret Bourke-White (copia a la gelatino-plata de 1937, positivada en la década de 1980; 5842 dólares), Niña en Gee’s Bend, Alabama de Arthur Rothstein (copia a la gelatino-plata de 1937, positivada hacia 1980; 4826 dólares), y Gastando el dinero de la recolección de algodón un sábado por la noche, apostando cerca de Clarksdale, Misisipi de Marion Post Wolcott (copia a la gelatino-plata virada al selenio de 1939, positivada en 1977; 3960 dólares), así como obras de Berenice Abbott, Jack Delano, Walker Evans y Ben Shahn.

Lecturas relacionadas:

Dorothea Lange y la fotografía como herramienta de cambio social Más allá de la madre migrante: cinco fotógrafos de la FSA que debes conocer

Retrato y Bellas Artes

David Wu Ject-Key, Mujer con blusa rosa, óleo sobre lienzo. Vendido por 11 220 dólares.

El retrato sobresalió con fuerza dentro de la selección de bellas artes, destacando Mujer con blusa rosa de David Wu Ject-Key, óleo sobre lienzo (11 220 dólares); Sin título (Retrato de una mujer afroamericana) de Gertrude Abrams Shilbey, óleo sobre lienzo, hacia principios de la década de 1940 (7620 dólares); Retrato de Moses Soyer de Raphael Soyer, óleo sobre lienzo (7920 dólares); y Mujer con blusa blanca de Moses Soyer, óleo sobre lienzo (6096 dólares). Otras obras originales incluyeron Sin título (Paisaje fauvista) de Hendrik Glintenkamp, óleo sobre lienzo, 1919 (8255 dólares); Naturaleza muerta de Jack Tworkov, óleo sobre lienzo (5588 dólares); y Reparadores de redes de Leon Bibel, óleo sobre lienzo, 1938 (5080 dólares).

Lecturas relacionadas:

Los artistas de la WPA y los albores de una nueva identidad americana Los artistas de la WPA: la promesa de un nuevo acuerdo (New Deal)

Grabados de Bellas Artes

Leon Bibel, Descendiendo, serigrafía a color, 1938. Vendido por 10 160 dólares.

La sección de obra gráfica de bellas artes incluyó serigrafías a color de Leon Bibel: Descendiendo, 1938 (10 160 dólares frente a una estimación de 2000 a 4000 dólares); Alto río Harlem, 1939 (7112 dólares); y Arco, 1939 (2540 dólares). Harry Sternberg, Charles Turzak, Blanche Grambs y Will Barnet también obtuvieron excelentes resultados.

Lecturas relacionadas:

Grabados en la historia: los grabadores del Proyecto de Arte Federal

Harold Porcher, especialista de la subasta y director de arte moderno y de posguerra en Swann, concluyó sobre el evento: «En tiempos de incertidumbre, identificar las futuras tendencias del mercado es un desafío. Parece que los compradores buscan esperanza en los artistas. A menudo, las respuestas a los momentos de incertidumbre residen en nuestro interior, y los fotógrafos, pintores, grabadores e ilustradores de la era del New Deal transmiten una sensación de adversidad y esperanza como pocos»

January 29, 2026

BY Kelsie Jankowski

Swann Galleries opened the year with an auction dedicated to The Artists of the WPA for the fifth year in a row. “The department and the material itself have come into their own,” noted Nicholas D. Lowry, Swann President. “During the sale, bidding was as frenetic and exciting as we have experienced in recent years, with active bidding in the room.” The sale brought $530,288, edging out its pre-sale estimate of $520,300 and selling 87% of the lots. “It would be easy to say that we have been doing our job well and are reaping the benefits of all the attention we have been paying to this underserved section of the art marketplace, however it is also very possible to imagine that the heart and soul of the WPA movement and specifically the Federal Art Project (where the government put artists to work to help fight the Depression), is being appreciated again, by those in a new era. It certainly feels like the efforts of the New Deal are being enjoyed by a modern audience for the same reason this art was so compelling when it was created—but now with a much more nostalgic twist,” Lowry concluded.

FSA Photography

Dorothea Lange, Migrant Mother, Nipomo, California, silver print, 1936, printed 1970s. Sold for $13,970.

The auction was led by Dorothea Lange’s iconicMigrant Mother, Nipomo, California, silver print, 1936, printed 1970s, at $13,970. Additional FSA photography included Margaret Bourke-White’sThe American Way of Life (At the Time of the Louisville Flood, Kentucky), silver print, 1937, printed 1980s ($5,842), Arthur Rothstein’sGirl at Gee’s Bend, Alabama, silver print, 1937, printed circa 1980 ($4,826), and Marion Post Wolcott’sSpending cotton picking money on Saturday nite, gambling near Clarksdale, Mississippi, selenium-toned silver print, 1939, printed 1977 ($3,960), as well as works by Berenice Abbott, Jack Delano, Walker Evans, and Ben Shahn.

Related Reading:

Dorothea Lange & Photography as a Tool for Social Change Beyond Migrant Mother: Five FSA Photographers to Know

Portraiture & Fine Art

David Wu Ject-Key, Woman in Pink Blouse, oil on canvas. Sold for $11,220.

Portraiture was a strong stand out among the fine art selection, with David Wu Ject-Key’s Woman in Pink Blouse, oil on canvas ($11,220), Gertrude Abrams Shilbey’s Untitled (Portrait of an African American Woman), oil on canvas, circa early 1940s ($7,620), Raphael Soyer’s Portrait of Moses Soyer, oil on canvas ($7,920), and Moses Soyer’s Woman in a White Blouse, oil on canvas ($6,096). Further original works include Hendrik Glintenkamp’s Untitled (Fauvist Landscape), oil on canvas, 1919 ($8,255), Jack Tworkov’sStill Life, oil on canvas ($5,588), and Leon Bibel’sNet Menders, oil on canvas, 1938 ($5,080).

Related Reading:

Artists of the WPA & the Dawn of a New American Identity The Artists of the WPA: The Promise of a New Deal

Fine Art Prints

Leon Bibel, Descending, color screenprint, 1938. Sold for $10,160.

Fine art prints included color screenprints by Leon Bibel:Descending, 1938 ($10,160 against a $2,000 to $4,000 estimate); Upper Harlem River, 1939 ($7,112);andArchway, 1939 ($2,540). Harry Sternberg, Charles Turzak, Blanche Grambs and Will Barnet also performed strongly.

Related Reading:

Etched in History: Printmakers of the Federal Art Project

Harold Porcher, specialist for the sale and director of Modern & Post-War art at Swann, concluded of the auction, “In times of uncertainty, identifying future auction trends is challenging. It seems buyers are looking to artists for hope. Often, we know the answers to uncertain times in our heart, and the photographers, painters, printers, and illustrators of the New Deal era convey feelings of hardship and hope like few others”

BY Kelsie Jankowski

2025 was yet another year filled with big sales and unique items for Swann. Single-owner collection included February’s Abstract Beauty: The Patricia Scipio-Brim Collection, the April auction of Art Deco at 100: William Crouse Collection, and the Reba W. & Dave H. Williams Collection of Color Woodcuts sold in April and October. Stand-out lots included autograph letters signed by George Washington and American Revolution material throughout our Books & Manuscripts offerings, anticipating America’s 250th birthday. Fine Photographs and Fine Art featured strong results for women practitioners, including works by Clara Etso Ugbodaga-Ngu, Berenice Abbott, Blanche Lazzell, Alma Thomas, and more.

Fotografías finas en Swan Traiga $1.1M con Steve McCurry Niños Haciendo su debut en la subasta

Swann Galleries’ October 16, 2025, sale of Fine Photographs trajo $1.1M y estableció dos registros de subastas. De la directora del departamento de venta, Deborah Rogal, señaló:

“Estamos encantados con los resultados de nuestra subasta Fine Photographs, que mostró fuerza y competencia en todo y demostró el entusiasmo constante por la fotografía entre los coleccionistas. Con resultados emocionantes para el trabajo de Steve McCurry, Ruth Orkin, Ansel Adams, Hiroshi Sugimoto, y muchos otros, así como un registro para el W. Eugene Smith Saipan (dos soldados), la venta mostró una amplia gama de practicantes y médiums. La diversidad, relevancia y accesibilidad de la fotografía continúan impulsando el éxito de nuestras ventas”.

Registros de subastas: Steven McCurry " W. Eugene Smith

Steve McCurry, Niños, portafolio completo con 10 impresiones Fuji Flex Crystal Archive, 1992-2001, impreso en 2010. Vendido por $35,560.

La rara cartera de Steven McCurry Niños, una de una edición de cinco, y completa con 10 fotografías llamativas, incluyendo Afghan Girl, alrededor de 1992-2001, impreso 2010, hizo su debut en subasta. El trabajo icónico trajo $33,560.

W. Eugene Smith’sSaipan (dos soldados), la impresión de plata, 1944, impreso en 1950, estableció un registro para la imagen en $33,020, contra una estimación de $5,000 a $7,500.

Portraiture

Herb Ritts, Torso roto, Los Angeles, Platinum print, 1989. Vendido por $16,510.

La retrato fue liderada por Su RittsWrapped Torso, Los Angeles, impresión platino, 1989, a $16,510. Otros trabajos incluyeron el de Richard AvedonAndy Warhol, Artista, Nueva York, 8-20-69, impresión de plata, 1969, impreso 1975, a $10,160, Robert MapplethorpePhillip Prioleau (en un pedestal), impresión de plata, 1979, a $9,525, y George Platt LynesYul Brynner, impresión de plata, 1951, a 8.890 dólares.

Beyond Fashion: Fotografias en una categoría Overlooked en el Lexicon de Bellas Artes

Ansel Adams & Landscape Photography

Las imágenes de Ansel Adams de la Sierra Nevada estaban entre los mejores lotes de la venta, con Sierra Nevada, Winter, del Valle de Owens, California, impresión en plata, 1944, impreso en diciembre de 1978, yWinter Sunrise, Sierra Nevada, de Lone Pine, California, impresión en plata, 1944, impreso en abril de 1978, ganó $33,020 cada uno.

Carleton E. Watkins, Distant View of the Domes, mammoth albumen print, 1865-66. Vendido por $13,970.

Fotografía paisajística adicional incluida Carleton E. Watkins’Vista distante de las Domas, mamut albumen print, 1865-66, a $13,970, Sebastião SalgadoElephant (contra la luz), Parque Nacional Kafue, Zambia, estampado de plata, 2010, a $9,525, Edweard MuybridgeDescanso de la nube, Valle del Yosemite (No 40), mamut albumen print, 1872, a $6,858, y la cartera de Eliot Porter con 12 de 12 impresiones de transferencia de tintes Dos: Islandia, 1975, a $6,604.

Five Photographers Who Used Environmental Photography as an Art Form

Mira: Five Photographers Who Used Environmental Photography as an Art Form with Alice le Campion

Escenas de ciudades

Ruth Orkin, American Girl in Italy (Ninalee Craig), impresión plateada, 1951, impreso en 1980.

Las escenas de la ciudad y la vida diaria incluyeron la de Ruth OrkinAmerican Girl in Italy (Ninalee Craig), impresión de plata, 1951, impreso 1980, que ganó $25.400 y Eugène Atget Coiffeur, Avenue de l’Observatoire , París, Aristóteles, a $25,400. También de la nota fue Lewis W. Hine Welders on the Empire State Building, impresión de plata, alrededor de 1930, que trajo $15,240, y El 67th Street, Nueva York, impresión en plata, 1955, impreso más tarde, a 8.890 dólares.

Fotografía de color contemporáneo

Fotografía de color incluido Lucas SamarasFoto-transformación 11/5/73, único SX-70 Polaroid, 1973, vendido por $15,240, Harold Edgerton’sVer el No visto: Doce fotografías de Harold Edgerton, portafolio con 12 fotografías, cinco transferencias de tintes y siete impresiones de plata, a $13,200, y Barbara KastenPintura fotogénico 74, cianotipo único, fotograma de vandyke, 1974, a $12,065.

Hiroshi Sugimoto, Rosecrans Drive-In, Paramount, estampado de plata, 1993. Vendido por $21,590.

Hiroshi Sugimoto fue la estrella de la oferta contemporánea con Rosecrans Drive-In, Paramount, impresión en plata, 1993, ganando $21,590, yPalms, Michigan, impresión de plata, 1980, que trae $ 19.050. George Tice Estación de Mobil y Watertower de Petit, Cherry Hill, N.J., estampado en plata de selenio, 1974, impreso en 1988, también fue popular con los coleccionistas, vendiendo por $11,430.

October 16, 2025

BY Kelsie Jankowski

Fine Photographs at Swann Bring $1.1M with Steve McCurry’s Children Making its Auction Debut

Swann Galleries’ October 16, 2025, sale of Fine Photographs brought $1.1M and established two auction records. Of the sale department director, Deborah Rogal, noted:

“We are delighted with the results of our Fine Photographs auction, which showed strength and competition throughout and demonstrated the continued enthusiasm for photography among collectors. With thrilling results for work by Steve McCurry, Ruth Orkin, Ansel Adams, Hiroshi Sugimoto, and many others, as well as a record for the W. Eugene Smith Saipan (two soldiers),the sale showcased a broad range of practitioners and mediums. Photography’s diversity, relevance, and accessibility continue to drive the success of our sales.”

Auction Records: Steven McCurry & W. Eugene Smith

Steve McCurry, Children, portfolio complete with 10 Fuji Flex Crystal Archive prints, 1992-2001, printed 2010. Sold for $35,560.

Steven McCurry’s rare portfolio Children, one of an edition of five, and complete with 10 striking photographs, including Afghan Girl, circa 1992-2001, printed 2010, made its auction debut. The iconic work brought $33,560.

W. Eugene Smith’sSaipan (two soldiers), silver print, 1944, printed 1950s, set a record for the image at $33,020, against a $5,000 to $7,500 estimate.

Portraiture

Herb Ritts, Wrapped Torso, Los Angeles, Platinum print, 1989. Sold for $16,510.

Portraiture was led by Her Ritts’Wrapped Torso, Los Angeles, platinum print, 1989, at $16,510. Further works included Richard Avedon’sAndy Warhol, Artist, New York City, 8-20-69, silver print, 1969, printed 1975, at $10,160, Robert Mapplethorpe’sPhillip Prioleau (on a pedestal), silver print, 1979, at $9,525, and George Platt Lynes’Yul Brynner, silver print, 1951, at $8,890.

Ansel Adams & Landscape Photography

Ansel Adams’ images of the Sierra Nevada were among the top lots of the sale, with Sierra Nevada, Winter, from the Owens Valley, California, silver print, 1944, printed December 1978, andWinter Sunrise, Sierra Nevada, from Lone Pine, California, silver print, 1944, printed April 1978, earned $33,020 each.

Carleton E. Watkins, Distant View of the Domes, mammoth albumen print, 1865-66. Sold for $13,970.

Additional landscape photography included Carleton E. Watkins’Distant View of the Domes, mammoth albumen print, 1865-66, at $13,970, Sebastião Salgado’sElephant (against light), Kafue National Park, Zambia, silver print, 2010, at $9,525, Edweard Muybridge’sCloud’s Rest, Valley of the Yosemite (No 40), mammoth albumen print, 1872, at $6,858, and Eliot Porter’s portfolio with 12 of 12 dye transfer prints Two: Iceland, 1975, at $6,604.

City Scenes

Ruth Orkin, American Girl in Italy (Ninalee Craig), silver print, 1951, printed 1980.

City scenes and daily life included Ruth Orkin’sAmerican Girl in Italy (Ninalee Craig), silver print, 1951, printed 1980, which earned $25,400, and Eugène Atget’s Coiffeur, Avenue de l’Observatoire , Paris, aristotype, at $25,400. Also of note was Lewis W. Hine’s Welders on the Empire State Building, silver print, circa 1930, which brought $15,240, and El 67th Street, New York, silver print, 1955, printed later, at $8,890.

Contemporary & Color Photography

Color Photography included Lucas Samaras’Photo-transformation 11/5/73, unique SX-70 Polaroid, 1973, sold for $15,240, Harold Edgerton’sSeeing the Unseen: Twelve Photographs by Harold Edgerton, portfolio with 12 photographs, five dye transfer and seven silver prints, at $13,200, and Barbara Kasten’sPhotogenic Painting 74, unique cyanotype, vandyke photogram, 1974, at $12,065.

Hiroshi Sugimoto, Rosecrans Drive-In, Paramount, silver print, 1993. Sold for $21,590.

Hiroshi Sugimoto was the star of the contemporary offering with Rosecrans Drive-In, Paramount, silver print, 1993, earning $21,590, andPalms, Michigan, silver print, 1980, bringing $19,050. George Tice’s Petit’s Mobil Station and Watertower, Cherry Hill, N.J., selenium-toned silver print, 1974, printed 1988, was also popular with collectors, selling for $11,430.

Deborah Rogal, Director:

Fan Ho’s Brief Encounter, 1960

Fan Ho, Brief Encounter, silver print, 1960s. Estimate $2,000 to $3,000.

“Fan Ho’s atmospheric and deeply humanist photographs of the streets and inhabitants of Hong Kong in the 1950s and 60s appeal to me for their fine detail, flawless compositions, and resonant storytelling. Largely self-taught, Ho’s work manages to convey Hong Kong during a period of growth and transformation while appealing to a sense of timeless nostalgia, both poetic and evocative. I love the use in this composition of the open window’s form replicated in the luminous lanterns and the lit window high above, as well as the wealth of detail that can be found in the dark tones of the buildings. Even the narrow gutter glows next to the textured street, and the man’s beautifully delineated shadow reaches toward our central character, the momentarily still cat. It is easy to imagine the man speaking softly as he approaches the animal.

This striking light study from Carlotta Corpron’s later series Space Compositions, ca. 1945–50, exemplifies her investigation of how light creates the illusion of space and depth. While deceptively simple at first glance, the still life reveals refined complexity. By staging everyday objects, Corpron transforms them into a study of light refraction and geometric interplay. Corpron was a groundbreaking pioneer of American abstract photography. Even though interest in her work has waned in recent decades, a retrospective of her work will be on view at the Smithsonian’s Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden in 2026. Her presence on the secondary market remains rare, making this print a significant example of her later-period work.

Bridget Fay,Cataloguer and Client Relations:

Carrie Mae-Weems, Untitled (Woman and Daughter with Makeup), from the Kitchen Table Series, 1990; printed 1999

Carrie Mae Weems, Untitled (Woman and Daughter with Makeup), from the Kitchen Table Series, silver print, 1990; printed 1999. Estimate $2,500 to $3,500.

Many are moved by Carrie Mae Weems’ photographs, and this is no exception.As part of its full Kitchen Table Series, it tells a choreographed domestic story where Weems sets herself as a subject and narrator within a fictional life, examining the nuances of life, love, and identity. As an individual print, the story being told is up to interpretation in our mind as the viewer. Our own lives and experiences shape the way we see and what we take away from the scene. While Weems remains calm and stoic, applying her lipstick, the dramatic lighting evokes a somber feeling, contrasting with the child shadowing her in play.

A Alice Le Campion

Descubre cinco fotógrafos que han modelado el reconocimiento de la fotografía ambiental como forma de arte. Estos artistas han dedicado su práctica a la belleza del mundo natural y redefinido la forma en que la naturaleza se presenta a través de su visión artística y habilidades técnicas, pero también han utilizado la fotografía como una herramienta para promover la conciencia ambiental.

Carleton Watkins

Carleton E. Watkins, Sección del Gigante Grizzly, Mariposa Grove, Yosemite-Sección-de-Grizzly-Giant-?saleno=2684 limitNo=3 limitrefNo=823755), 1861.

Carleton Watkins fue uno de los primeros en fotografiar la majestuosidad del Oeste Americano. A principios de 1861, Watkins visitó el Parque Nacional Yosemite y capturó su belleza intacta utilizando dos tipos de cámaras: una enorme cámara de mamut-plate para capturar detalles nítidos, y una cámara estereoscópica para captar profundidad. Estos paisajes fueron en gran medida invisibles, incluso desconocidos, por el público en ese momento.

Se dice que las imágenes influenciaron al presidente Abraham Lincoln para firmar el Yosemite Grant en 1864, una pieza histórica de legislación que allanaría el camino para la creación del sistema nacional del parque. De las muchas montañas en Yosemite, el Monte Watkins fue nombrado después de Carleton. Hoy, estas impresionantes impresiones de albumen siguen siendo un testigo asombroso de un tiempo pasado de un intrépido Occidente americano.

Ansel Adams

Ansel Adams, Salida de la luna, Hernández, Nuevo México-Moonrise-Hernandez-New-Mexico?saleno=2406 implicalotNo=99 curvarefNo=714549), estampado de plata de tamaño mural, 1941, reprocesado 1948, impreso a principios de mediados de 1950. Vendido febrero 2016 por $221,000.

Ansel Adams siguió el camino de Watkins más de 50 años más tarde cuando visitó por primera vez el Parque Nacional Yosemite en 1916 con su familia a los 14 años. Adams fue un defensor temprano y largo tiempo para la conservación y protección ambiental del desierto, y un miembro del Club Sierra, una de las primeras agencias de conservación ambiental a gran escala.

Sus puntos de vista escénicos de Occidente han sido ampliamente reproducidos y están entre las imágenes más icónicas conocidas tanto por el público como por la comunidad de arte. Y es cierto decir que además de sus cualidades artísticas, han sido instrumentales para concienciar sobre la necesidad de preservar nuestras maravillas naturales.

Fue galardonado con la Medalla Presidencial de la Libertad en 1980 por el Presidente Carter, quien declaró, “A la belleza de los monumentos de la naturaleza, él (Ansel Adams) es considerado por los ambientalistas como un monumento mismo, y por los fotógrafos como una institución nacional. Es a través de su previsión y fortaleza que tanto de América ha sido salvada para los futuros estadounidenses”.

Su imagen de Los Tetons y el río Snake, 1942, fue incluido en el Registro de Oro de la nave Voyager lanzado al espacio en 1977 como una de las 116 imágenes que representan a la humanidad.

Eliot Porter

Eliot Porter, imagen de Portafolio Dos: Islandia-Portfolio-Two-Iceland?saleno=2426 PullotNo=150 curvafNo=721911), 12 fotografías de la flora variada y exuberante y vibrantes paisajes de Icealnd, grabados en transger, 1972, impreso en 1975.

Influido profundamente por el naturalista Henry David Thoreau, Eliot Porter viajó por todo el mundo para captar la diversidad ecológica de nuestro mundo. Sus proyectos han sido publicados en forma de numerosos libros y carteras, algunos de ellos en colaboración directa con el Sierra Club, uno de los grupos ambientales más influyentes fundados en 1892, incluyendo su obra maestra de 1962 En la naturaleza es la preservación del mundo.

También fue pionero en la fotografía de color, y influyó profundamente en los cimientos de la fotografía de la naturaleza tal como lo conocemos hoy. Es especialmente conocido por utilizar la técnica de impresión de transferencia de tintes, que más le agradaba hacer la belleza de la naturaleza a través de colores ricos y vibrantes. Ansel Adams lo describió como un “maestro del color de la naturaleza” que trajo credibilidad a la fotografía de color como un medio de arte fino.

Sebastião Salgado

Sebastião Selgado, Pingüinos de Chinstrap en la Isla Zavodovski, Islas Sandwich del Sur-Chinstrap-Penguins-on-Zavodovski-?saleno=2659 limitlotNo=25 limitrefNo=813717), impresión plateada, 2009. Vendido 2024 febrero por $18,750.

Sebastião Salgado es conocido por sus proyectos documentales a largo plazo centrados en temas sociales y ecológicos. De sus proyectos altamente aclamados, Trabajadores documentos de trabajo manual industrial, mientras Migraciones cubre el tema del desplazamiento de la población en masa. Génesis, a la que Salgado se refirió como su “carta de amor al planeta”, pasó ocho años entre 2004 y 2012 viajando por el mundo para capturar una impresionante imagen de ambientes naturales prístinos y las comunidades de personas que los habitan.

Además de trabajar como fotógrafo, Salgado se ha comprometido durante muchos años a proteger el medio ambiente. En 1998, él y su esposa establecieron el Instituto Terra, un proyecto de reforestación en su Brasil natal.

Salgado, que falleció recientemente, se recuerda por su capacidad de capturar tanto la belleza como las duras realidades del mundo con igual calidad artística a través de la combinación de sorprendente composición en blanco y negro e iluminación dramática.

Nick Brandt

Nick Brandt, Retrato de elefante en polvo, Amboseli-Portrait-of-Elephant-in-Dust-Amboseli-(?saleno=2385 PullotNo=382 limitrefNo=704231), de A través de la tierra devastada, parte I, impresión de pigmento de archivo, 2011. Vendido mayo 2015 por $ 46.800.

El amor de Nick Brandt por la vida silvestre fue revelado mientras trabajaba en Tanzania en un proyecto de video para Michael Jackson La canción de la Tierra En 1995, a diferencia de la mayoría de los fotógrafos de fauna silvestre, Brandt nunca utilizó el telefoto ni lentes de zoom, sino lentes cortas. Al verse forzado a acercarse a sus sujetos, creó estos icónicos retratos de primer plano de la fauna africana utilizando el medio ambiente como su estudio.

Brandt amplió su práctica artística a lo largo de los años a proyectos que retratan tanto a animales como a personas afectadas por el cambio climático en todo el mundo. El día puede romperse (2021-2024) ha tenido lugar hasta ahora en Zimbabwe, Kenya, Bolivia, Fiji y Jordania. Al investigar proyectos relacionados con el impacto destructivo causado por la humanidad, Brandt tiene por objeto dar visibilidad a los afectados.

En 2010, Nick Brant cofundó Big Life Foundation con el conservacionista Richard Bonham, dedicado a preservar y proteger los animales salvajes de África Oriental y su ecosistema.

Estos fotógrafos han moldeado el campo de la fotografía ambiental y son una fuente continua de inspiración para fotógrafos y conservacionistas por igual.

BY Alice Le Campion

Discover five photographers who shaped the recognition of environmental photography as an art form. These artists have devoted their practice to the beauty of the natural world and redefined the way nature is portrayed through their artistic vision and technical skills, but they also have used photography as a tool to advocate for environmental awareness.

Carleton Watkins

Carleton E. Watkins, Section of the Grizzly Giant, Mariposa Grove, Yosemite-Section-of-the-Grizzly-Giant-?saleno=2684&lotNo=3&refNo=823755), 1861.

Carleton Watkins was one of the first to photograph the majesty of the American West. As early as 1861, Watkins visited Yosemite National Park and captured its untouched beauty by using two types of cameras: a huge mammoth-plate camera to capture crisp detail, and a stereoscopic camera to capture depth. These landscapes were largely unseen, even unknown, by the public at the time. Not only did his photographs reveal their beauty to a wider audience, but they also unveiled the necessity of preserving such untamed natural areas.

It is said that the images influenced President Abraham Lincoln to sign the Yosemite Grant in 1864, a landmark piece of legislation that would pave the way for the creation of the national park system. Of the many mountains in Yosemite, Mount Watkins was named after Carleton. Today, these stunning albumen prints remain an amazing witness to a time past of an untouched American West.

Ansel Adams

Ansel Adams, Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico-Moonrise-Hernandez-New-Mexico?saleno=2406&lotNo=99&refNo=714549), mural-sized silver print, 1941, reprocessed 1948, printed early- to mid-1950s. Sold February 2016 for $221,000.

Ansel Adams followed Watkins’s path more than 50 years later when he first visited Yosemite National Park in 1916 with his family at the age of 14. Adams was an early and longtime advocate for wilderness conservation and environmental protection, and a member of the Sierra Club, one of the first large-scale environmental preservation agencies.

His scenic views of the West have been widely reproduced and are amongst the most iconic images known both by the public and the art community. And it is true to say that besides their artistic qualities, they have been instrumental in raising awareness about the necessity of preserving our natural wonders.

He was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1980 by President Carter, who stated, “Drawn to the beauty of nature’s monuments, he (Ansel Adams) is regarded by environmentalists as a monument himself, and by photographers as a national institution. It is through his foresight and fortitude that so much of America has been saved for future Americans.”

His image of The Tetons and the Snake River, 1942, was included on the Voyager spacecraft’s Golden Record launched into space in 1977 as one of the 116 images representing humankind.

Eliot Porter

Eliot Porter, image from Portfolio Two: Iceland-Portfolio-Two-Iceland?saleno=2426&lotNo=150&refNo=721911), 12 photographs of the varied and lush flora and vibrant landscapes of Icealnd, dye transger prints, 1972, printed 1975.

Deeply influenced by the naturalist Henry David Thoreau, Eliot Porter traveled around the globe to capture the ecological diversity of our world. His projects have been published in the form of numerous books and portfolios, some of them in direct collaboration with the Sierra Club, one of the most influential environmental groups founded in 1892, including his 1962 masterpiece In Wildness is the Preservation of the World.

He was also a pioneer in color photography, and he profoundly influenced the foundations for nature photography as we know it today. He is particularly known for using the dye transfer printing technique, which suited him most to render the beauty of nature through rich and vibrant colors. Ansel Adams described him as a “master of nature’s color” who brought credibility to color photography as a medium of fine art.

Sebastião Salgado

Sebastião Selgado, Chinstrap Penguins on Zavodovski Island, South Sandwich Islands-Chinstrap-Penguins-on-Zavodovski-?saleno=2659&lotNo=25&refNo=813717), silver print, 2009. Sold February 2024 for $18,750.

Sebastião Salgado is known for his long-term documentary projects focusing on social and ecological issues. Of his highly acclaimed projects, Workers documents industrial manual labor, while Migrations covers the topic of mass population displacement. For his third opus, entitled Genesis, which Salgado referred to as his “love letter to the planet”, he spent eight years between 2004 and 2012 traveling the world to capture a striking portrayal of pristine natural environments and the communities of people who inhabit them.

Besides working as a photographer, Salgado has been committed for many years to protecting the environment. In 1998, he and his wife established the Instituto Terra, an ongoing reforestation project in his native Brazil.

Salgado, who recently passed away, is remembered for his ability to capture both the beauty and harsh realities of the world with equal artistic qualities through the combination of striking black-and-white composition and dramatic lighting.

Nick Brandt

Nick Brandt, Portrait of Elephant in Dust, Amboseli-Portrait-of-Elephant-in-Dust-Amboseli-(?saleno=2385&lotNo=382&refNo=704231), from Across the Ravaged Land, Part I, archival pigment print, 2011. Sold May 2015 for $46,800.

Nick Brandt’s love for wildlife was revealed while he was working in Tanzania on a video project for Michael Jackson’s Earth Song in 1995. Unlike most wildlife photographers, Brandt never used telephoto or zoom lenses but short lenses. Being forced to get closer to his subjects, he created these iconic close-up portraits of the African wildlife by using the environment as his studio.

Brandt expanded his artistic practice over the years to projects portraying both animals and people affected by climate change around the world. His ongoing global series entitled The Day May Break (2021-2024) has so far taken place in Zimbabwe, Kenya, Bolivia, Fiji, and Jordan. By investigating projects related to the destructive impact caused by humankind, Brandt aims to give visibility to those impacted.

In 2010, Nick Brant co-founded Big Life Foundation with conservationist Richard Bonham, dedicated to preserving and protecting the wild animals of East Africa and their ecosystem.

These photographers have shaped the field of environmental photography and are an ongoing source of inspiration for photographers and conservationists alike.
